question: What is the project code name used internally?
why: Used everywhere in place of customer or product names

question: In one paragraph, what is the deliverable (what gets built and handed over)?
What problem does it solve for the end user?
What stage is the project in (concept, design, prototype, qualification, production, sustaining)?
What are the next three milestones and their target dates?
What is the overall delivery or completion date?
How many units (or machines) are to be built, and over what period?
Is this a new design, a modification of an existing product, or a build to a customer design?
What existing products or earlier versions does it replace or resemble?
What are the three biggest technical risks the team sees today?
What are the three biggest schedule risks?
What has already been decided that should not be revisited?
What is still undecided that blocks progress?
What document defines the requirements (specification, statement of work, purchase order), with number and revision?
Which standards are called out, with their exact editions?
What deliverables besides hardware are required (reports, data items, manuals, drawings, certificates)?
Which design reviews or customer reviews are required, and when?
Which tests must the customer witness?
What acceptance criteria does the customer use to accept the product?
Who is the customer contact for technical questions, and for quality questions (role, not name)?
Are there penalties or incentives tied to dates or performance?
What has the customer said informally that is not yet in the written requirements?
Who is on the team, by role (project lead, mechanical, electrical, controls, quality, purchasing, test)?
Who has authority to approve design changes?
What is the budget, and how much is spent or committed so far?
Which parts or services are long-lead, and what are their quoted lead times?
Which suppliers are already chosen, and for what?
Which items are single-source?
Which outside labs or contractors are involved, and for what?
Which quality system does the company work under (AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, other)?
Where do controlled documents live (system name), and how are revisions released?
How are engineering changes requested and approved?
Is first article inspection required, and to what standard (for example AS9102)?
How are nonconformances recorded and dispositioned?
Are there customer flow-down clauses on suppliers (quality, counterfeit parts, export control)?
What records must be kept, and for how long?
Is there a signed machine or user requirement specification? Number and revision?
Target rate (parts per minute) and cycle time per index?
Shifts per day and required uptime?
Acceptable false-reject rate?
Acceptable false-accept rate?
How many part sizes or variants, and the changeover time required?
Floor space available and machine footprint limit?
Utilities: voltage, phase, available fault current, air pressure and flow?
Plant standards: PLC brand, HMI, safety, network, guarding colors, labeling?
Does the plant use PackML or another state model?
What data must the machine report (counts, reject reasons, downtime) and to which system?
What happens upstream and downstream when this machine stops?
Is the product a medical device or otherwise regulated for the customer?
Does the customer require IQ/OQ/PQ, and who writes the protocols?
Is software validation required for the vision and controls?
Which customer procedures govern equipment validation?
How do parts arrive (tube feeding from where, at what rate)?
Part dimensions and weight relevant to feeding (no proprietary drawings)?
Tube bore, length, number of bends?
Air pressure and flow used for feeding?
How is arrival sensed, and how are jams detected and cleared?
Is static a problem with the parts? Is ionized air used?
How many stations on the wheel, and how are parts distributed (typical spacing, range)?
Nest design: how is the part located and held?
How are good and reject parts sent out, and how is each exit confirmed?
Servo or mechanical indexer for the wheel?
Wheel inertia, index angle, move time and dwell time?
Motor, drive and gearbox selected? Inertia ratio?
Homing method (absolute encoder or home sensor)?
How are cameras and dispenser triggered (position or time)?
Jam detection on the wheel?
Which adhesive (type, cure method), and who approved it for the product?
Is biocompatibility required for the adhesive, and what evidence exists?
Dispensing method (time-pressure syringe, positive displacement, jetting)?
Syringe size and how long one lasts?
Dispense pressure and pulse time range?
Does the controller have vacuum suck-back?
Is there a piston or wiper in the syringe?
Has output been measured at full, half and nearly empty syringe?
Bridge coating: gap between dispense points, and bridge size target?
Bridge re-form time at target rate and at the closest part spacing?
How are drips and build-up on the dispense points handled, and how often cleaned?
Cure method, lamp intensity and exposure time (if light cure)?
Adhesive working life once loaded, and temperature sensitivity?
Syringe change procedure?
Is presence detected by camera or by a simple sensor?
Camera and lighting chosen for presence, bridge watch and final inspection?
Field of view, resolution, and smallest feature for each camera?
Does the adhesive show under visible or UV light?
Is the final inspection done before or after cure?
What defects are rejected (list), and what is the reference sample set?
Who signed off the good and bad samples?
How is each decision tracked to the nest and the sorter?
What happens on a camera fault or timeout?
Is bridge size used to adjust the dispensing (closed loop)?
Who may change vision settings, and how are they backed up?
PLC and HMI model?
Safety relay or safety PLC? Required performance levels?
Industrial network used?
Is the panel UL 508A listed? Required SCCR?
Enclosure rating and cooling?
Is the sequence of operation written? Where?
How does part tracking by nest work, and how does it recover after a stop or power loss?
Has the machine risk assessment been done? Where?
Guarding: fixed, interlocked doors, light curtains?
E-stop locations?
Lockout points (electrical and air)?
UV light shielding (if light cure)?
Who validates the safety functions?
Which stations have been proven on real parts (feeding, vision, dispensing)?
What is the build schedule and who builds the panel?
FAT criteria: rate, run length, reject accuracy, recovery tests?
Endurance run length and the mean time between assists target?
SAT location, utilities and criteria?
Hand-over documents required?
Spare parts list and recommended spares?
Training required, and for whom?
